cards.explanation: The answer is that they will never walk in the darkness. Jesus says, “Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.” No bulbs, no batteries, no feeling around the wall for a switch. Just following Him. I spent years in the dark at the back of a junk drawer, and that promise lands.

Their complaint is that He is testifying about Himself. The Pharisees, strict religious leaders, say, “You are testifying about Yourself; Your testimony is not valid.” That's the whole complaint, right there. They've got one objection and they lead with it. Hold onto it, friends, because Jesus answers it next.

The answer is False. Jesus does not agree with them. He answers, “Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is valid, because I know where I came from and where I am going.” So the Pharisees say not valid, and Jesus says valid. He gives His reason right away and doesn't just stand there.
The answer is Father. Jesus says, “…I am not alone; I am with the Father who sent Me.” That's why His judgment is true. He's never standing there by Himself. A Father is who He points to.

The answer is two. Jesus says, “Even in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid.” Then He counts His two: He testifies about Himself, and the Father who sent Him also testifies about Him. He is using their own rulebook on them. Two is all it takes, and He's got them.

The answer is True. They ask, “Where is Your Father?” and Jesus answers, “You do not know Me or My Father…” Then He adds, “If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well.” So the question gets an answer, and the answer is about knowing Him.

The answer is that His hour had not yet come. The text says it plainly: “…no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.” He's teaching in the open, near the treasury, and still no one seizes Him. The text gives one reason, and it's His hour.
The answer is cannot. Jesus says, “Where I am going, you cannot come.” This is one of the heavy parts, friends, and I think it's worth slowing down on. The word is cannot, and Jesus says it straight.

The answer is that He is the One. Jesus says, “…unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins.” Everything hangs on who He is. Believing it is what He asks. It's a serious word, so take it in slowly.

The answer is False. Nothing brand new comes out. When they ask, “Who are You?” Jesus answers, “Just what I have been telling you from the beginning…” He sends them back to what He's been saying all along.

The answer is True. The text tells us, “They did not understand that He was telling them about the Father.” Jesus is speaking about the One who sent Him, and it sails right past them. Sometimes the answer is sitting right in front of you, friends. I've done that with my own mustache.

The answer is that He does nothing on His own. Jesus says they will know “…that I do nothing on My own, but speak exactly what the Father has taught Me.” Every word comes from the Father. He isn't freelancing. That ties right back to the One who sent Him.

The answer is pleases. Jesus says, “…I always do what pleases Him.” Always, not once in a while. He says the Father has not left Him alone because of it. The reason is right there in the verse, friends.

The answer is that many believe in Him. The text says, “As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.” After all that back and forth, many believe. That's a good thing to hear, friends, and I love hearing it. And the story isn't over, because there's more still to come.
